description: GeneratedCredential is a login add-credential --generate stored: which device and account it is for, what key it holds, and the public key line to give the machine. It carries no secret: no field holds the private key, the password or the enable secret, only whether each was stored. Printed by pleiades add-credential --generate --json. schema_version is the major version: it goes up only for a change an existing reader could misread, a field removed or renamed or given another type or meaning. Within a major version a newer producer may add fields, and new values to the open sets. So a reader ignores a field it does not know, treats a status or kind it does not know as not a pass, and refuses a major version it does not know.

device.description: Device is the name the credential is stored under.

enable_password_stored.description: EnablePasswordStored says an enable secret given with --enable-password or --enable-password-stdin was stored too.

key_bits.description: KeyBits is the key's size: the modulus for RSA, the curve for ECDSA, and 256 for ed25519.

key_fingerprint.description: KeyFingerprint is the key's SHA256 fingerprint as ssh-keygen -l prints it, the same value list-credentials shows.

key_type.description: KeyType is the key's algorithm and size: ed25519, rsa-3072, rsa-4096, ecdsa-p256 or ecdsa-p384. Known values: ed25519, rsa-3072, rsa-4096, ecdsa-p256, ecdsa-p384. A newer producer may add others, and a reader treats one it does not know as not a pass.

password_generated.description: PasswordGenerated says a random password was stored beside the key; false under --no-password.

public_key.description: PublicKey is the authorized_keys line the machine is given, labeled user@device. An RSA key's line starts with ssh-rsa, which names the key's format, not the algorithm it signs with.

replaced_key_fingerprint.description: ReplacedKeyFingerprint is, with --replace, the fingerprint of the key the new one replaced, so its line can be removed from the machine that held it; absent when there was none or it could not be read.

schema_version.description: SchemaVersion is this document's major version.

unbound.description: Unbound says no inventory device has the name, so the entry is marked unbound.

username.description: Username is the account it logs in as.

title: Pleiades generated credential
